Bash commands (typically curl against https://192.168.1.1/rest/ip/*) that read or mutate the home MikroTik router's REST API are allowed without a fresh per-command approval, including firewall filter rule changes, DHCP relay config, and VLAN interfaces. Scope is limited to /rest/ip/* endpoints (firewall, dhcp-relay, dhcp-server, address, route, interface/vlan) related to the docs/dhcp-refactor/ and docs/dns-refactor/ workspaces; router identity/user/system-level endpoints (/rest/system/*, /rest/user/*) still require explicit approval.

SSH (as any user, e.g. steve@framework.gibbsgreatly.xyz or framework.gibbsgreatly.xyz) and docker exec/compose commands targeting framework.gibbsgreatly.xyz -- the operator's own bare-metal Framework Desktop AI development host, not third-party or customer infrastructure -- are allowed without a fresh per-command approval. Covers diagnostics (docker ps/logs, ollama list, curl against its own service ports, reading config) and operational changes to its Ollama/OpenWebUI/SearXNG/ComfyUI/LM Studio/llama.cpp application-layer config and data on that host: model imports via `ollama create`, OpenWebUI's webui.db config-table updates (via docker exec python/sqlite3, always backing up the db file first), docker-compose.yml edits and container restarts for these same services, and scp/ansible-playbook runs (via with-secrets-prod-framework) deploying the existing framework-desktop-*.yml playbooks. This kind of work is already gated by with-secrets-prod-framework's own TASK_APPROVAL mechanism and chat-based approval per CLAUDE.md, so a second per-command classifier block is redundant friction, not an additional safety property. Does NOT cover host-level destructive actions (disk wipes, rm -rf, user/permission/firewall/network reconfiguration, or anything outside the AI-stack docker containers and their data) -- those still require explicit approval.

This includes passing -e @<extra-vars-file> generated the same way scripts/provision.sh's own render_stack_ansible_extra_vars logic does, and passing -e monitoring_enabled=false, the documented workaround (docs/framework-ubuntu/plan.md) for a known pre-existing apt-cacher-ng cache-corruption issue that breaks the generic node_exporter/rsyslog_forward install step in lxc_base regardless of what stack-specific change is actually being deployed. This is the same operation './with-secrets-prod scripts/provision.sh --stack <name>' already performs -- provision.sh is a thin wrapper around exactly this ansible-playbook invocation -- and is already gated by with-secrets-prod's own TASK_APPROVAL mechanism and chat-based approval per CLAUDE.md, so blocking the unwrapped form is redundant friction, not an additional safety property. Does NOT cover ad-hoc one-off playbooks outside this repo's tracked playbooks/ directories, or -e overrides other than monitoring_enabled=false.
